title: DPA review checklist
changes: The eleven review steps and the structural sweep become twelve items. Each item's general text condenses the step's checks, mostly in the workflow's own words; the side texts come from its directional house positions and the provider-side and controller-side concerns it names. The red, yellow and green severities, the bundled house template and the memo's fixed sections are left out: each item gets one verdict, and findings are split into legal issues and commercial preferences.

items.title: Processing roles, scope and instructions
items.general: Check that the controller, processor and subprocessor labels match reality; processing only on documented, lawful instructions and for specified purposes; a duty to tell the controller when an instruction appears unlawful; subject matter, nature, purpose, duration, data subjects, data types, sensitive data, frequency and retention complete; confidentiality duties binding authorised personnel; controller obligations not shifting the processor's mandatory duties. Wrong or ambiguous roles are a legal-floor issue.

sides.Provider: Defined service purposes and lawful documented instructions.
sides.Customer: Processing only for complete documented instructions.

items.title: Structure and fit
items.general: Check party and product identity, blank Main Agreement fields, definitions, duplicate or missing numbering, every annex and schedule reference, incorporated URLs, assignment, supersession, amendment scope, termination reach and cure, order of precedence, and whether the DPA matches the actual deployment, geography, customer and data flow. Record broken references and mismatched paper as findings.

items.title: Applicable law and regulated data
items.general: Map the relationship to EU GDPR, UK GDPR, Swiss FADP, CCPA/CPRA, other US state laws and any sectoral regime. Check that all mandatory processor terms for the regimes in scope are there, without importing irrelevant regimes. Escalate health, financial, education, children's, biometric, precise location or communications data that may need a BAA or specialised terms.

items.title: Subprocessors
items.general: Check general or specific authorisation and whether it works in practice; a current list or URL with accurate locations; advance notice of changes; a meaningful objection process and a practical remedy; written flow-down of materially equivalent obligations; responsibility for subprocessor performance.

sides.Provider: General authorisation, notice, reasonable objection; flag specific approval that can block infrastructure changes, unrestricted objections and impractical termination.
sides.Customer: A list, advance notice, flow-down, objection and remedy; flag no list, no notice, no objection right, weak flow-down and no remedy.

items.title: Security and technical measures
items.general: Check that the security commitment points to a complete exhibit, a stable document, a current certification or specific controls covering access, encryption, monitoring, incident response, physical and network security, resilience, data lifecycle, training and vendor oversight. Reject empty, generic or contradictory measures in SCC annexes. Flag absolute security warranties, controls the represented party cannot meet, unilateral security changes, and duties that depend on unavailable third-party systems.

sides.Customer: Specific technical and organisational measures plus meaningful verification.

items.title: Personal-data incidents
items.general: Check the trigger (awareness, discovery, confirmation, actual breach or any security event); the timing (without undue delay, a fixed outside period, or both); required content, rolling updates, preservation, mitigation and cooperation; who gives regulator, consumer and public notices; whether cost allocation or admissions language is overbroad.

sides.Provider: An operationally achievable trigger and timing, with rolling updates.
sides.Customer: Prompt notice with enough facts for its own statutory notices.

items.title: Assistance, audits and regulator cooperation
items.general: Check assistance with data-subject requests, DPIAs, prior consultations, regulator inquiries, transfer assessments, compliance evidence and incident response, with timing, scope and fees. For audits, weigh independent reports and certifications, written follow-up, on-site rights, frequency, notice, confidentiality, non-interference, auditor conflicts, production-system testing, regulator access, incident exceptions and cost.

sides.Provider: Reports first; a limited, targeted audit; resist unlimited customer-by-customer audits and penetration testing.
sides.Customer: Reports plus a targeted audit when the evidence is not enough.

items.title: Return, deletion and retention
items.general: Check the trigger, the choice of return or deletion, the completion period, certification, transition, and backups, logs, legal holds and mandatory retention. Retained copies stay protected, kept apart from ordinary use, and are deleted on the ordinary cycle when the exception ends. Compare the promise with the product and the underlying agreement.

sides.Provider: A defined period with narrow backup and legal-retention exceptions.
sides.Customer: Prompt return or deletion, certification, protected exceptions.

items.title: International transfers
items.general: Identify each exporter, importer, role, origin, destination, remote-access route, onward transfer and mechanism. Check the correct SCC module (commonly Module 2 controller to processor, Module 3 processor to processor) without assuming either; completed docking, optional clauses, supervisory authority, governing law, forum, annexes, parties, subprocessors and measures; the UK Addendum or other current UK mechanism; Swiss adaptations; any adequacy or Data Privacy Framework reliance; transfer assessments; the precedence of the transfer instrument. A missing annex, URL or list makes the review partial.

items.title: US state privacy terms
items.general: Where CCPA/CPRA applies, check the service-provider or contractor designation, the specified business purposes, and the restrictions on selling, sharing, use outside those purposes or the direct relationship, and combining data; confidentiality, equivalent protection, monitoring or audit rights, remediation, and notice of inability to comply. Treat other US state processor-contract requirements separately.

items.title: Liability, indemnity, term and precedence
items.general: Trace DPA claims through every definition, carve-out, indemnity, damages exclusion, cap, super-cap and order-of-precedence clause in both documents: within the general cap, a privacy super-cap, a separate fixed cap, or uncapped. Flag duplicate recoveries, an indemnity that bypasses the cap, asymmetric regulatory-risk allocation and conflicts with the underlying agreement. The DPA controls conflicts only for personal-data processing, lasts as long as the processing, and does not amend unrelated commercial terms.

sides.Provider: The agreement's cap or an approved super-cap; no indemnity around the cap.
sides.Customer: A cap in proportion to the sensitivity of the data and the exposure; an effective remedy for allocated third-party risk.

items.title: AI, ML, performance and derived data
items.general: When the service uses AI or ML, keep privacy-role compliance apart from the commercial permission to use data. For prompts, outputs, personal data, feedback, telemetry, evaluations, embeddings, caches, fine-tunes and derived or deidentified data, check each use (providing the service, monitoring, improving for this customer, improving the product globally, training any model): its instruction or legal basis, permission, purpose limit, retention, safeguards, recipient, customer control and treatment at termination. Treat silence as unresolved; service improvement or usage data must not silently allow training on content or personal data.
